If a certain supplier's plan comes to fruition, some memory chips used in Apple devices will be manufactured in the United States for the first time.

According to the latest report, Apple's memory supplier SK hynix is in discussions with Intel, with the intention of using a chip fabrication plant that Intel plans to build in Ohio...

As reported by Reuters, although details remain unclear at this stage, this Korean company produces RAM and flash memory chips for Apple devices.

Processors used in some Apple devices are already manufactured in the United States, but due to restrictions on foreign companies from accessing TSMC's most advanced process nodes, these processors can only be used in older models. However, since Apple uses industry-standard versions, DRAM or NAND flash memory chips are not affected by such restrictions.

However, the report also pointed out that the plan may face opposition from the South Korean government, as South Korea may have similar concerns to Taiwan regarding the export of chip manufacturing technology, even when it involves older process nodes.

SK hynix stated that no decision has been made at this time. Intel declined to comment on the report, but confirmed that it will continue to push forward with the development plans for the Ohio project.
